metadata.description: Unified Ancient and Historical Genomic Data

WHG.name: Western Hunter-Gatherers
WHG.description: Mesolithic foragers who inhabited Europe before farming. Dark skin, blue eyes.

EHG.name: Eastern Hunter-Gatherers
EHG.description: Hunter-gatherers from the steppe and forest zones east of the Baltic.

ANF.name: Anatolian Neolithic Farmers
ANF.description: First farmers who migrated from the Near East, bringing agriculture to Europe.

Yamnaya.name: Yamnaya/Steppe Pastoralists
Yamnaya.description: Bronze Age herders who massively impacted European genetics. Brought Indo-European languages.

Neanderthal.name: Neanderthal
Neanderthal.description: Archaic humans who interbred with modern humans leaving ~1-4% DNA in non-Africans.

Denisovan.name: Denisovan
Denisovan.description: Archaic humans related to Neanderthals. Up to 5% DNA in some Melanesian populations.

AncientAfrican.name: Ancient African
AncientAfrican.description: Pre-Bantu hunter-gatherer and early agriculturalist lineages from West, East, and Southern Africa.

AncientEastAsian.name: Ancient East Asian / Paleo-Indian
AncientEastAsian.description: Pleistocene ancestors of East Asians and Native Americans who migrated across Beringia.

WHG.note: Blue eyes originated in WHG. Nearly all Mesolithic European hunter-gatherers had blue eyes.

EHG.note: Mixed - some blue, some brown eyes in eastern populations.

ANF.note: Brown eyes predominant in Neolithic farmers from Anatolia.

Yamnaya.note: Mixed eye colors in Steppe populations. Likely acquired from WHG admixture.

rs12913832.history: The blue eye mutation arose once in a single European ancestor ~6,000-10,000 years ago, during the Mesolithic. Hunter-gatherers had blue eyes but dark skin - a combination not seen in modern Europeans.

WHG.note: WHG had DARK SKIN despite living in Europe for 30,000+ years. This light skin allele was absent.

EHG.note: Some EHG carried the light skin allele, especially those with ANF admixture.

ANF.note: Neolithic farmers from Anatolia were already fixed for light skin.

rs1426654.history: Modern European light skin came from Neolithic farmers, NOT from adaptation in Europe. Hunter-gatherers were dark-skinned for 30,000+ years. The light skin allele swept through Europe only after ~5,000 BCE with farming.

WHG.note: Some WHG carried this light skin variant, but not fixed.

rs16891982.history: This second major European light-skin gene has a different history than SLC24A5. It was partially present in hunter-gatherers and increased through Bronze Age migrations.

WHG.note: No lactase persistence - could not digest milk as adults.

EHG.note: Lactase persistence absent in pre-pastoral populations.

ANF.note: SURPRISINGLY, early farmers could NOT digest milk! They kept animals for meat, not dairy.

Yamnaya.note: Only ~10-20% carried the allele initially. Despite herding, most Steppe people were lactose intolerant.

rs4988235.history: Lactase persistence only became common in the last 4,000 years - much later than domestication. It underwent one of the strongest selective sweeps in the human genome, going from <5% to >70% in Northern Europeans in just 100 generations.

rs3827760.trait: Hair thickness, shovel-shaped incisors, sweat glands

WHG.note: European hunter-gatherers did not have this East Asian variant.

ANF.note: Not present in Near Eastern farmers.

AncientEastAsian.note: Selected in East Asian populations, possibly for cold adaptation or other factors.

rs3827760.history: This variant underwent strong selection in East Asia ~30,000 years ago. It affects multiple traits: thick straight hair, shovel-shaped incisors (common in Native Americans and East Asians), and increased sweat gland density.

WHG.note: European hunter-gatherers susceptible to Plasmodium vivax malaria.

ANF.note: Near Eastern farmers did not have malaria resistance.

AncientAfrican.note: Fixed or near-fixed in sub-Saharan Africa for thousands of years.

rs2814778.history: The Duffy-null allele provides complete resistance to Plasmodium vivax malaria. It reached near-fixation in sub-Saharan Africa where malaria was endemic. This is one of the clearest examples of selection by infectious disease.

AncientEastAsian.note: Dry earwax variant highly selected in East Asian populations.

rs17822931.history: The dry earwax allele is nearly fixed in East Asian and Native American populations, suggesting strong selection ~40,000 years ago. It also reduces apocrine gland secretion (less body odor). The selective pressure is unknown - possibly cold adaptation or social selection.

WHG.note: Associated with blue eye color in hunter-gatherers.

rs4778241.history: Part of the OCA2/HERC2 eye color locus. Multiple variants in this region interact to produce blue, green, and brown eye colors.

rs1800407.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Fair skin & red hair pigmentation

introgression.effect: Reduces MC1R receptor signaling, contributing to fair skin

rs1800407.history: Neanderthal MC1R loss-of-function allele identified in European Neanderthals.

Neanderthal.note: This haplotype is derived from Neanderthal introgression.

rs72921001.history: This region shows clear Neanderthal introgression and may affect pain sensitivity. Only present in populations with Neanderthal ancestry (non-Africans).

introgression.effect: Enhanced antiviral response

rs10774671.history: The Neanderthal version of OAS1 provides enhanced protection against RNA viruses. It was likely positively selected in modern humans after introgression.

introgression.effect: Modified innate immune response

rs35744605.history: TLR1 variants from Neanderthals affect how the innate immune system responds to bacteria. These variants are among the most strongly positively selected Neanderthal introgressions.

Neanderthal.note: Complex introgression history at this locus.

introgression.effect: Altered xenobiotic metabolism

rs2066853.history: The AHR gene regulates the body's response to environmental toxins and is involved in detoxification. Neanderthal variants may reflect adaptation to different diets or environments.

Neanderthal.note: Neanderthal haplotype associated with lighter skin.

introgression.effect: Lighter skin, freckling, sun sensitivity

rs7277176.history: BNC2 is a major determinant of skin color and freckling. The high frequency of this Neanderthal variant in Europeans suggests strong positive selection for lighter skin at high latitudes.

rs1881227.history: This region contains one of the most well-characterized Neanderthal introgression haplotypes in modern Europeans.

rs1042602_anc.history: TYR variants affect melanin production. Selection at this locus contributed to European skin pigmentation adaptation.

introgression.effect: Prevents polycythemia at extreme high altitude (Tibetan Plateau)

rs1427656.history: Introgressed from Denisovans into the ancestors of Tibetans ~40,000 years ago. Allows normal oxygen transport without hyper-viscous blood at high altitudes.

rs73885319.trait: Denisovan introgression - Adipose fat distribution & cold adaptation

introgression.effect: Drives brown fat differentiation and metabolic heat generation

rs73885319.history: Denisovan-derived haplotype that regulates body fat distribution and adaptation to extreme cold in Greenlandic Inuit and Indigenous Americans.

rs1042531.trait: Denisovan introgression - Innate immune receptor response

introgression.effect: Enhanced toll-like receptor sensing of bacterial pathogens

rs1042531.history: Shared archaic immune haplotype present in Denisovans and early modern humans in Asia and Oceania.

rs11724015.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Keratinocyte skin barrier defense

introgression.effect: Increased epidermal skin thickness and keratin differentiation

rs11724015.history: High-frequency Neanderthal introgression in East Asians that provided protection against northern UV and environmental skin pathogens.

rs13097409.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Pigmentation & red hair variant

introgression.effect: Reduced MC1R activity leading to fair skin and red hair

rs13097409.history: Functional MC1R loss-of-function mutation identified in Altai Neanderthals, contributing to fair skin adaptation.

introgression.effect: Lowers hemoglobin concentration at extreme altitude, preventing polycythemia

rs143758366.history: Intronic EPAS1 variant introgressed from Denisovans into ancestors of Tibetans ~40,000 years ago.

rs2298080.trait: Denisovan introgression - Adipose fat distribution & cold adaptation

introgression.effect: Alters brown adipose tissue differentiation and body fat distribution

rs2298080.history: Denisovan-derived developmental gene variant selected in Greenlandic Inuit and Indigenous Americans.

introgression.effect: Influences skin pigmentation and freckling in non-African populations

rs10756819.history: Neanderthal introgression locus in BNC2 under strong positive selection in West Eurasians.

rs2066807.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Type-I Interferon antiviral signaling

introgression.effect: Alters STAT2 interferon transcription and immune defense against viruses

rs2066807.history: Missense Neanderthal STAT2 variant introgressed into Eurasian and Melanesian ancestors.

rs13342232.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Lipid metabolism & Type-2 diabetes risk

introgression.effect: Alters hepatic lipid metabolism and increases type-2 diabetes risk

rs13342232.history: Neanderthal coding variant in SLC16A11 common in Latin American and Native American populations.

introgression.effect: Modulates thiamine transport and neuro-metabolism

rs4804803.history: Neanderthal regulatory variant affecting vitamin B1 metabolism.

introgression.effect: Modulates mucin 19 expression in respiratory tract

rs11568800.history: Neanderthal introgression region affecting mucosal immune defense.

rs34684178.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Vocal tract & language development region

introgression.effect: Modulates FOXP2 non-coding regulatory sequences

rs34684178.history: Archaic non-coding FOXP2 haplotype shared between Neanderthals and modern Eurasians.

rs10994397.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Gut immunity & Crohn's disease risk

introgression.effect: Alters mucosal immune regulation in intestinal tract

rs10994397.history: Neanderthal introgression locus associated with inflammatory bowel disease risk.

rs1048971.trait: Neanderthal introgression - B-cell complement receptor 2 response

introgression.effect: Alters complement receptor 2 (CD21) binding affinity

rs1048971.history: Neanderthal missense variant in CR2 under immune selection.

introgression.effect: Modulates extracellular matrix remodeling and height

rs715585.history: Neanderthal introgression variant influencing skeletal phenotype.

rs174570.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Polyunsaturated fatty acid desaturation

introgression.effect: Alters arachidonic and linoleic acid metabolic conversion

rs174570.history: Neanderthal fatty acid desaturase variant adaptive for cold climate lipid diets.

rs1047643.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Zinc transport & neuronal homeostasis

introgression.effect: Alters neuronal zinc transporter function

rs1047643.history: Neanderthal missense mutation in SLC30A9 (ZnT9) influencing zinc homeostasis.

introgression.effect: Modulates serine/threonine kinase 33 expression

rs1233078.history: Neanderthal introgression locus expressed during male gametogenesis.

introgression.effect: Alters oxysterol production and viral entry suppression

rs34814041.history: Neanderthal immune variant enhancing lipid-mediated antiviral defense.

rs1018596.trait: Neanderthal introgression - Intestinal mucin barrier defense

introgression.effect: Modulates intestinal epithelial glycoprotein shield

rs1018596.history: Neanderthal introgression marker protecting gut epithelium from pathogens.

loschbour.name: Loschbour Man
loschbour.description: A famous Western Hunter-Gatherer. Known to have had dark skin, dark hair, but bright blue eyes.

cheddar_man.name: Cheddar Man
cheddar_man.description: Oldest complete skeleton found in Britain. Typical WHG phenotype of dark skin and light eyes.

stuttgart.name: Stuttgart
stuttgart.description: An Early European Farmer of the LBK culture. Brought agriculture from Anatolia. Had light skin and brown eyes.

anzick.name: Anzick-1
anzick.description: The only known human burial associated with the Clovis culture. Closely related to modern Native Americans.

luzia.name: Luzia (Lagoa Santa)
luzia.description: One of the oldest human skeletons found in South America. Her genome confirms early Paleoamerican migration continuity shared across Indigenous South Americans.

usr1.name: Upward Sun River 1 (USR1)
usr1.description: An infant genome from interior Alaska representing Ancient Beringians—the earliest diverged lineage of ancient Americans prior to Northern/Southern Native American splits.

lovelock_cave.name: Lovelock Cave Ancestor
lovelock_cave.description: Ancient Great Basin inhabitant demonstrating direct genetic lineage continuity with modern Numic-speaking populations (Paiute and Shoshone).

lauricocha.name: Lauricocha Highland Ancestor
lauricocha.description: One of the earliest high-altitude Andean genomes, showing early adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia and genetic continuity with modern Quechua populations.

machu_picchu.name: Machu Picchu Inca Royal Ancestor
machu_picchu.description: Late pre-Columbian imperial Inca genome from the Royal Estate of Machu Picchu, exhibiting highland Quechua and coastal Peruvian genetic components.

fuegian_yamana.name: Fuegian Yámana Ancestor
fuegian_yamana.description: Ancient southern maritime hunter-gatherer from Tierra del Fuego representing the extreme southern terminus of ancient human expansion into South America.

tianyuan.name: Tianyuan Man
tianyuan.description: Landmark 40,000-year-old human from Tianyuan Cave near Beijing. Demonstrates early divergence of East Asian lineages from Western Eurasian populations.

jomon.name: Jōmon Hunter-Gatherer
jomon.description: Indigenous hunter-gatherer of the Japanese archipelago prior to Yayoi agricultural expansion. Characterized by wet earwax, dark skin, and unique island adaptation.

rakhigarhi.name: Rakhigarhi Indus Valley Ancestor
rakhigarhi.description: High-coverage genome from the Harappan civilization. Predates Steppe pastoralist migration into South Asia, representing ancient Ancestral South Indian (ASI) baseline.

kostenki14.name: Kostenki-14 (Markina Gora)
kostenki14.description: Early European hunter-gatherer genome. Shows deep shared ancestry between Western Hunter-Gatherers and Ancient North Eurasians.

boncuklu.name: Boncuklu Anatolian Farmer
boncuklu.description: Pre-Pottery Neolithic inhabitant of central Anatolia, ancestral to the Early European Farmers who brought agriculture to Europe.

australian_ancient.name: Ancient Australian (Willandra Lakes)
australian_ancient.description: Ancient Aboriginal Australian genome demonstrating 50,000+ years of genetic isolation and deep lineage continuity in Sahul.

mota.name: Mota
mota.description: The first ancient African genome sequenced. Predates the Eurasian backflow into Africa.

yamnaya_samara.name: Yamnaya Herder
yamnaya_samara.description: Nomadic pastoralists from the Pontic-Caspian steppe who expanded massively during the Bronze Age.

mota_ethiopia.name: Mota Man
mota_ethiopia.description: A hunter-gatherer from the Mota Cave. His genome predates the massive migration of Eurasian farmers into East Africa.

shum_laka_cameroon.name: Shum Laka Boy
shum_laka_cameroon.description: Key for understanding the origins of Bantu-speaking populations and West African hunter-gatherers.

i8088_catoctin.name: Catoctin Ancestor (I8088)
i8088_catoctin.description: Part of an enslaved community at a Maryland iron furnace. Shows mixed Wolof, Kongo, and British Isles ancestry. A direct link to African American ancestral history.

ghk_sudan.name: Kulubnarti Nubian
ghk_sudan.description: Nubian samples that show the complex mix of Nilotic and Near Eastern lineages in the Nile Valley.

taforalt_morocco.name: Taforalt Individual
taforalt_morocco.description: The oldest Iberomaurusian genome. Shows a link between Near Eastern and Sub-Saharan African lineages.

nama_san_deep.name: Deep San Ancestor
nama_san_deep.description: Represents the world's oldest genetic lineages. This individual shows continuity with modern Nama and San groups, with signatures that have remained stable for over 10,000 years.

anzick_1.name: Anzick-1 (Clovis Boy)
anzick_1.description: Skeletal remains of an infant boy buried with Clovis stone tools in Montana. His genome confirms the Siberian migration origin of Native Americans and shows direct lineage continuity with modern Indigenous Central and South Americans.

kennewick_man.name: Kennewick Man (Ancient One)
kennewick_man.description: Found along the Columbia River. A landmark legal and genetic case that proved close genetic continuity to the modern Colville and other Pacific Northwest Native American tribes.

gyamfi_single.name: Gyamfi Single
gyamfi_single.description: An ancient West African genome from Ghana predating the major Bantu migration events, providing a key baseline of historic West African genetic variation.

luxor_ancestor.name: Luxor Ancient Egyptian
luxor_ancestor.description: Ancient Egyptian from a mummified community. Shows high genetic affinity to historical Near Eastern and Anatolian populations with smaller Sub-Saharan African components.

rameses_iii.name: Rameses III
rameses_iii.description: Famous pharaoh of the 20th Dynasty, known for repelling the Sea Peoples during the Late Bronze Age collapse.

richard_iii.name: King Richard III
richard_iii.description: The last English monarch of South-Western Europe descent to die in battle, found buried under a car park in Leicester.

malta_boy_ma1.name: Mal'ta Boy (MA-1)
malta_boy_ma1.description: Landmark 24,000-year-old genome defining Ancient North Eurasian (ANE) ancestry. MA-1 contributed ~30-40% ancestry to all Indigenous Americans and ~40-50% to Bronze Age Steppe herders.

villabruna_whg.name: Villabruna WHG
villabruna_whg.description: Cornerstone reference genome for Western Hunter-Gatherers (WHG). Represented post-glacial blue-eyed, dark-skinned European foragers who expanded across Mesolithic Europe.

satsurblia_chg.name: Satsurblia CHG
satsurblia_chg.description: Reference genome for Caucasus Hunter-Gatherers (CHG). Provided the critical second ancestral lineage (alongside EHG) that coalesced into Yamnaya Steppe herders.

oetzi_iceman.name: Ötzi the Iceman
oetzi_iceman.description: Europe's oldest known natural human mummy. Carried Y-haplogroup G2a and high Anatolian Farmer ancestry, suffering from lactose intolerance and atherosclerosis.

sunghir_paleolithic.name: Sunghir Upper Paleolithic Ancestor
sunghir_paleolithic.description: Famous Gravettian-era burial site near Moscow. Represents early European Upper Paleolithic foragers with complex burial rituals and thousands of mammoth ivory beads.

oase_1.name: Oase 1 (Peștera cu Oase)
oase_1.description: One of the oldest modern human fossils found in Europe. Possesses ~6–9% recent Neanderthal ancestry from interbreeding just 4 to 6 generations back in his family tree.

denisova_3.name: Denisova 3 (Denisovan Hominin)
denisova_3.description: High-coverage finger bone genome defining Denisovans—an archaic human lineage whose DNA persists in Oceanian, Southeast Asian, and East Asian populations.

chagyrskaya_neanderthal.name: Chagyrskaya Neanderthal
chagyrskaya_neanderthal.description: High-coverage Neanderthal genome representing Micoquian toolmakers closely related to Neanderthals who interbred with the ancestors of non-Africans.

guanche_canary.name: Guanche Ancestor
guanche_canary.description: Indigenous inhabitant of the Canary Islands before European colonization. Displays genetic affinity to ancient North African Berbers.

bichon_man.name: Bichon Man
bichon_man.continent: Grotte du Bichon, La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland
bichon_man.description: Azilian hunter-gatherer found alongside a brown bear. Represents late Epipaleolithic Western Hunter-Gatherers prior to farming.

shum-laka-cameroon.name: Shum Laka Boy
shum-laka-cameroon.description: Key for understanding the origins of Bantu-speaking populations and West African hunter-gatherers.

i8088-catoctin.name: Catoctin Ancestor (I8088)
i8088-catoctin.description: Part of an enslaved community at a Maryland iron furnace. Shows mixed Wolof, Kongo, and British Isles ancestry. A direct link to African American ancestral history.

ghk-sudan.name: Kulubnarti Nubian
ghk-sudan.description: Nubian samples that show the complex mix of Nilotic and Near Eastern lineages in the Nile Valley.

taforalt-morocco.name: Taforalt Individual
taforalt-morocco.description: The oldest Iberomaurusian genome. Shows a link between Near Eastern and Sub-Saharan African lineages.

nama-san-deep.name: Deep San Ancestor
nama-san-deep.description: Represents the world's oldest genetic lineages. This individual shows continuity with modern Nama and San groups, with signatures that have remained stable for over 10,000 years.

spirit_cave_mummy.name: Spirit Cave Mummy
spirit_cave_mummy.description: The oldest natural mummy found in North America. Genetic sequencing confirmed close lineage continuity with modern Indigenous groups, resolving long-standing controversies.

ballito_bay.name: Ballito Bay Child
ballito_bay.description: An ancient hunter-gatherer child whose high-coverage genome proved Khoe-San lineages diverged over 260,000 years ago, predating modern out-of-Africa migrations.

asselar_man.name: Asselar Man
asselar_man.description: A skeleton from the 'Green Sahara' wet phase of West Africa, representing crucial Holocene-era baseline variation prior to the Sahara's desertification.

otzi.name: Ötzi the Iceman
otzi.description: Natural mummy preserved in ice. Neolithic farmer with brown eyes and light skin.

viking_denmark.name: Viking Warrior (Galgedil)
viking_denmark.description: Viking Age warrior showing typical Scandinavian profile and lactase persistence.

catoctin_iron_workers.name: Catoctin Iron Workers
catoctin_iron_workers.description: Genetic markers associated with enslaved individuals from Catoctin Furnace, Maryland.

western_hunter_gatherer.name: Western Hunter-Gatherer (WHG)
western_hunter_gatherer.description: Representative markers for West European Hunter-Gatherer ancestry.

early_european_farmer.name: Early European Farmer (EEF)
early_european_farmer.description: Representative markers for Early European Farmer ancestry.

mota-ethiopia.name: Mota Man
mota-ethiopia.description: A hunter-gatherer from the Mota Cave. His genome predates the massive migration of Eurasian farmers into East Africa.

clusters.name: New York African Burial Ground (NYABG)
clusters.description: An estimated 15,000 individuals were interred here. These lineages represent the founding African community of New Amsterdam/New York.

clusters.name: St. Helena 'Liberated Africans'
clusters.description: Intercepted by the Royal Navy during the final phase of the slave trade, these 27,000 individuals represent a direct genomic fingerprint of 19th-century West-Central Africa.

clusters.name: Takarkori 'Green Sahara' Ghost
clusters.description: A deeply divergent lineage from the 'Green Sahara' that remained isolated for millennia. Represents a 'Ghost Population' distinct from modern groups.

matches.description: Key for understanding the origins of Bantu-speaking populations and West African hunter-gatherers.

matches.name: Catoctin Ancestor (I8088)
matches.description: Part of an enslaved community at a Maryland iron furnace. Shows mixed Wolof, Kongo, and British Isles ancestry. A direct link to African American ancestral history.

matches.name: Kulubnarti Nubian
matches.description: Nubian samples that show the complex mix of Nilotic and Near Eastern lineages in the Nile Valley.

matches.name: Taforalt Individual
matches.description: The oldest Iberomaurusian genome. Shows a link between Near Eastern and Sub-Saharan African lineages.

matches.name: Deep San Ancestor
matches.description: Represents the world's oldest genetic lineages. This individual shows continuity with modern Nama and San groups, with signatures that have remained stable for over 10,000 years.

matches.name: Spirit Cave Mummy
matches.description: The oldest natural mummy found in North America. Genetic sequencing confirmed close lineage continuity with modern Indigenous groups, resolving long-standing controversies.

matches.name: Ballito Bay Child
matches.description: An ancient hunter-gatherer child whose high-coverage genome proved Khoe-San lineages diverged over 260,000 years ago, predating modern out-of-Africa migrations.

matches.name: Asselar Man
matches.description: A skeleton from the 'Green Sahara' wet phase of West Africa, representing crucial Holocene-era baseline variation prior to the Sahara's desertification.

matches.name: Ötzi the Iceman
matches.description: Natural mummy preserved in ice. Neolithic farmer with brown eyes and light skin.

matches.name: Viking Warrior (Galgedil)
matches.description: Viking Age warrior showing typical Scandinavian profile and lactase persistence.

matches.name: Catoctin Iron Workers
matches.description: Genetic markers associated with enslaved individuals from Catoctin Furnace, Maryland.

matches.name: Western Hunter-Gatherer (WHG)
matches.description: Representative markers for West European Hunter-Gatherer ancestry.

matches.name: Early European Farmer (EEF)
matches.description: Representative markers for Early European Farmer ancestry.

matches.name: Mota Man
matches.description: A hunter-gatherer from the Mota Cave. His genome predates the massive migration of Eurasian farmers into East Africa.
